Thirty years after Tupac Shakur's murder, a trial seeks to resolve a never-closed case
subhead: The trial of Duane 'Keefe D' Davis, accused of organizing and participating in the 1996 murder of rapper Tupac Shakur, begins on Monday, August 10, in Las Vegas. No one has ever been convicted in this case, which stands as one of the most famous cold cases in American history.

title: Golden relay double for Britain at European Championships as Marchand takes silver
subhead: French swim star Léon Marchand took silver on the opening day of the European swimming championships. Marchand has had to cut back on his events this week due to a lingering thigh injury, though he is still entered in the 200m butterfly and 400m freestyle.

title: Tunisia, country of broken dreams: 'I wanted to photograph the young people whose lives began with the revolution'
subhead: 'Growing up in hostile environments' (3/7). Tunisian photographer Zied Ben Romdhane has documented his country since the fall of Ben Ali and the Arab Spring in late 2010. His work captures the deep malaise of a generation that has known only political turmoil and a lack of economic opportunities. Deprived of hope, on the edge of a sun-drenched sea, these young people dream solely of leaving.

Gaza mourns during 'largest collective funeral in Palestinian history'
subhead: The remains of 112 people belonging to the same family, killed by an Israeli strike on a residential building in the Palestinian enclave, were buried on August 4, two and a half years after their deaths. Palestinians lack the resources to search for and recover the thousands of bodies still trapped beneath the rubble.

title: The French far-right fighters of the Lebanese Civil War
subhead: Despite their lack of military experience, in 1976, several young French far-right militants, eager for adventure, took up arms in Lebanon alongside Christian Phalangists during the civil war. The story has become a legend in their political camp.

title: 'Why shouldn't I have the right to do what Angelina Jolie did?': Inside a breast surgery clinic in Paris
subhead: 'My Breasts and Me' (1/5). For aesthetic, social, medical or political reasons, some women want smaller breasts, or none at all – a growing number of requests that simply did not exist some 15 years ago. Le Monde spent several weeks at the Paris Breast Center Restitute to understand this changing trend.
